They differ in what survives. `structuredClone` keeps Dates, Maps, Sets, typed arrays and `undefined`, and handles circular references, while the JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, Maps/Sets into `{}`, drops `undefined` and functions, and throws on cycles. Neither copies class prototypes, and `structuredClone` throws on functions where JSON silently drops them. Action: look at the line the reviewer flagged to see what shape of data it copies, and if it's not plain JSON-safe data, swap it to `structuredClone` and reply on the PR.

`as const` changes the inferred type to literal and readonly values and checks nothing. `satisfies` checks the value against a type but keeps the precise inferred type, so you get typo and missing-key errors without widening. You can combine them: `as const satisfies Config`. Action: none needed; the per-file TODO breakdown is still running in the background.

`using x = getResource()` calls `x[Symbol.dispose]()` automatically when the enclosing block exits, whether by return, break or throw, and multiple `using` declarations dispose in reverse order. `await using` does the same with `Symbol.asyncDispose` for async cleanup. It needs the runtime to have `Symbol.dispose` (or a polyfill) and the right `lib`/target setting, so I'd check our Node version before using it. Action: if you want to use it somewhere real, point me at the resource (DB client, file handle) and I'll sketch it.
